snp4.6:1.2: You die this side of a century,
snp4.6:1.3: but even if you live past,
snp4.6:2.1:
People grieve
for what they see as mine,
snp4.6:2.2:
for nothing possessed is constant,
nothing is constantly possessed.
snp4.6:2.3:
Seeing this separation
simply as it is,
one shouldn’t follow the household life.
snp4.6:3.4:
shouldn’t incline
to be devoted to mine-ness.
snp4.6:4.1:
Just as a man doesn’t see
on awakening
snp4.6:4.2: what he met in a dream,
snp4.6:4.4:
when they are dead
—their time done—
those he held dear.
snp4.6:5.2: people are called by this name or that,
snp4.6:5.3:
but only the name remains
to be pointed to
snp4.6:6.2:
lamentation, & selfishness
are not let go
by those greedy for mine,
snp4.6:6.4:
letting go of possessions,
go about
seeing the Secure.
snp4.6:7.3: They say it’s congenial for him,
snp4.6:7.4:
he who wouldn’t, in any realm,
display self.
snp4.6:8.4:
like water on a white lotus,
do not adhere.
snp4.6:9.1: As a water bead on a lotus leaf,
snp4.6:9.2: as water on a red lily,
snp4.6:9.3:
doesn’t adhere,
so the sage
doesn’t adhere
snp4.6:9.4: to the seen, the heard, or the sensed;
snp4.6:10.2:
in connection
with the seen, the heard, or the sensed.
snp4.6:10.3:
In no other way
does he wish for purity,
snp4.6:10.4:
for he neither takes on passion
nor puts it away.
